config.description: Runs lines of the CLI of the KiSS server {hostname} on {platform}, one command per line, as one batch that applies whole or not at all, the way Cisco IOS reads them: set <module> <key> [item] <value>, no <module> <key> [item], show <module>, show running-config [all], show startup-config, show diff <config> <config>, show version, show logging, copy running-config startup-config or write memory, erase running-config or erase startup-config, show conversations, erase <id> of a conversation or erase conversations for every one not pinned, a copy, a write or an erase asking the user's yes with a card of the page. Its modules, with their keys: {modules}. Every default fits as it is, so set only what differs. A secret never shows: show writes ! <module> <key> [item] is set for one that is set, and no line for one that is not. To set a secret, write its line without the value, set proxy key <name>: the user types it in a field you never see, so never ask for it in the chat. A url no configuration holds yet asks the user to let it with a card of the page as the line runs: run the line, never ask in the chat first.

description.description: Why I'm configuring the server, written first

client_config.description: Runs lines of the CLI of the KiSS page {client}, a browser attached to this server, on its own configuration: its endpoints, model, system prompt, tools, display, style and every other setting of the page, none of this server. One command per line, as one batch that applies whole or not at all, the way Cisco IOS reads them: set <module> <key> [item] <value>, no <module> <key> [item], show <module>, show running-config [all], show startup-config, write memory; show running-config all lists every module and key the page has. The page runs the lines itself and answers with what changed; a secret, a url to let or a yes it asks the user on the page.

view.description:
Supports viewing text, images, and directory listings on {hostname}.

Supported path types:
- Directories: Lists files and directories up to 2 levels deep, ignoring hidden items and the contents of node_modules
- Image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP): Displays the image visually
- Text files: Displays numbered lines. You can optionally specify a view_range to see specific lines.

modules.chat: the model the agent of this server answers with, endpoint/model, empty for the one model of the one endpoint, and its system prompt
modules.endpoints: the LLM endpoints the agent of this server talks to: the url, the protocol it speaks, the key and the header that carries it, Header or Header: Scheme, more headers, the seconds it may stay silent, the times a reply is asked again on a status that passes and the seconds between two
modules.files: the tools on files, view, str_replace and create_file: the bytes of text view returns, the bytes of a file a tool loads whole, the megapixels an image decodes to, the longest side and the JPEG quality of an image made again
modules.mcp: the MCP servers whose tools the agent of this server calls, over Streamable HTTP: the url, the key and the header that carries it, Header or Header: Scheme, more headers, the seconds a call may take; each tool of theirs takes tools use by its name, consent unless set
modules.models: the parameters of a model, the item endpoint/model, each sent only when set
modules.proxy: the servers this server proxies, MCP servers and LLM endpoints alike, each at proxy/<name> with the key of this server, the page by set mcp proxy or set endpoints proxy <name> <its name for this server>; the key of a route goes to its url alone, in the header its auth-header names, Header or Header: Scheme, and a route without a key reaches its url without one
modules.server: this server: where it listens, its hostname, which names its tools, the key its clients send off loopback, the directory its tools start in, its log level
modules.shells: a tool per shell whose program this machine has, named after the shell: the command reading a script on stdin, its seconds, its bytes of output
modules.tools: the tools the agent of this server calls, each by its own name on this server (bash, view, config): off, the model never sees it, consent, each call asks the user, on; and the rounds of tool calls a turn takes at most
